rule: Default block-goal size per test (e.g. lifts +7.5% e1RM, DB press +5%, pull-ups +25%, threshold pace -3%, 2k row +3%, broad jump +3%).
summary: No source sets block-goal sizes. Trial data give a sense of scale: national-level athletes gained 2.9-6.5% in 1RM squat over 10 weeks, so +7.5% e1RM per block is ambitious for a trained lifter, though more realistic while the athlete rebuilds. Concurrent training does not blunt maximal-strength gains but does blunt explosive gains (relevant to the +3% broad jump). Several goals sit close to test noise: row 3% vs about 2-2.5% error, threshold 3% vs 2-2.7%, DB press 5% vs 4% error plus 5-6% dumbbell jumps. A single retest cannot confirm those goals, so say so when one is chosen.

sources.note: Lindberg 2021: 10 weeks of strength/power training in national-level athletes gave 2.9-6.5% 1RM squat, 3-6% CMJ.
Concurrent training: maximal strength not compromised, explosive strength attenuated (SMD -0.28).
Hopkins 2000: judge an individual's change against the typical error; changes within noise are not interpretable.
